builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
summary: The method replaces per-step invocations of a large LLM for routine enumerable decisions with a single 4B System-1 model that resolves them in one forward pass, escalating to the large model only below a calibrated confidence threshold. The cost is an offline pipeline that mines decision points from over 1,000 skills, collects execution-grounded trajectories in isolated containers, and trains the 4B pointer model, plus an extra local model to host at run time. Failure modes include miscalibrated thresholds causing either silent wrong decisions or excessive fallback to the large model, and degraded coverage on workflows whose decision points differ from those represented in the mined skill corpus.
rationale: The 75-91% cost reduction is directly relevant to a constrained budget, but adopting AnyS1 requires reproducing an offline pipeline (skill mining, containerized trajectory collection, training a calibrated 4B pointer model) rather than calling an existing artifact, so the gain must be validated on the reader's own workflows before commitment.
technique: Small System-1 router for agent decision points

claims.statement: The method replaces per-step invocations of a large LLM for routine enumerable decisions with a single 4B System-1 model that resolves them in one forward pass, escalating to the large model only below a calibrated confidence threshold. The cost is an offline pipeline that mines decision points from over 1,000 skills, collects execution-grounded trajectories in isolated containers, and trains the 4B pointer model, plus an extra local model to host at run time. Failure modes include miscalibrated thresholds causing either silent wrong decisions or excessive fallback to the large model, and degraded coverage on workflows whose decision points differ from those represented in the mined skill corpus.
Cuts episode cost by 75-91% and model-call time by 63-92% versus an uncompiled System-2 agent, while preserving task reliability across three unseen benchmarks.
